questions.question: Explain why cocoa is grown in West Africa but not in South Africa.
questions.expected_answer: Cocoa trees need a hot, wet climate all year round with plenty of rain and no frost, which is found in tropical areas within about twenty degrees of the equator, such as Côte d'Ivoire and Ghana in West Africa. South Africa is mostly too dry and too cold in winter for cocoa.

questions.question: Describe the main steps from cocoa beans to chocolate.
questions.expected_answer: Farmers cut ripe pods, scoop out the beans and pulp, ferment them for about a week and dry them in the sun. The beans are sold, shipped to factories, cleaned, roasted and shelled. The nibs are ground into cocoa mass, some of which is pressed into cocoa butter and powder. Cocoa mass and cocoa butter are mixed with sugar and milk, smoothed, moulded into slabs, wrapped and sent to shops.

questions.question: Explain how value is added from cocoa to chocolate and who earns most of the money.
questions.expected_answer: Each step, including transporting, roasting, grinding, mixing, moulding, wrapping, advertising and selling, adds value, so chocolate is worth much more than the raw beans. Most of the money goes to the factories, brand owners, transport companies and shops, while cocoa farmers often receive only a small share, by some estimates less than a tenth.
